title: Cognisance the flower of quiet, margerain gentle
html_source:
To Mistress Margery Wentworth
- John Skelton. 1460?–1529

WITH margerain gentle,
The flower of goodlihead,
Embroidered the mantle
Is of your maidenhead.
Plainly I cannot glose;
Ye be, as I divine,
The pretty primrose,
The goodly columbine.

Benign, courteous, and meek,
With wordes well devised;
In you, who list to seek,
Be virtues well comprised.
With margerain gentle,
The flower of goodlihead,
Embroidered the mantle
Is of your maidenhead.

In Elizabethan herbals, margerain (marjoram) was the herb of calm and gentleness, a remedy for diseases of the brain. - Gifford
